source_boundary_notes: NCCP Child–Pugh C considers 75%; current product information does not recommend severe hepatic use. Explicit source-conflict hold/review, no numeric prescription.
Count thresholds are ANC ≥1 AND platelets ≥75×10⁹/L.
HFS is separate from general grade 1–2 toxicity; active grade 2/3 holds, with recurrence-specific reduction after recovery.
Symptomatic LVEF decline discontinues; asymptomatic decline delays until recovery.
Actual dose history is required for 12.5-mg reductions; usual minimum 25 mg.
Shared RCC national indication code should be 00325b; current internal route/code metadata left unchanged for parent integration.

Dose-range review: doses above the standard 50 mg/day require explicit prescription/interaction review; the GIST/RCC unavoidable-CYP3A4-inducer exception is at most 87.5 mg/day. Values above 87.5 mg/day are held for verification, even with an inducer. No numeric dose is automatically issued.

indications.description: Unresectable/metastatic GIST after imatinib failure or intolerance.
Advanced renal-cell carcinoma treated with sunitinib on a 4-weeks-on/2-weeks-off schedule.

treatment.schedule_summary: Sunitinib 50 mg orally once daily on Days 1–28, followed by 14 days off (Days 29–42); repeat 42-day cycles until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Take with or without food. Skip a missed dose; take the usual dose next day and never double.

hfs_grade.label: Current hand–foot syndrome (clinician-assessed CTCAE grade)
hfs_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess the current hand–foot syndrome severity. Assess skin changes, pain and limitation of instrumental versus self-care activities. The CTCAE v5.0 hand–foot descriptor is an explicitly labelled UI orientation aid; NCCP 00325 v6 does not specify a grading edition. Reconcile the clinician-assessed grade with the NCCP source action; never silently change source thresholds.
